# Combinatorics and Optimization reading group | Arkaprava Choudhury, Proof of the Sunflower Conjecture

Monday, October 26, 2026 11:00 am - 12:00 pm EDT (GMT -04:00)

iCal

Speaker:  | Arkaprava Choudhury
Affiliation:  | University of Waterloo
Room:  | MC 6029

Abstract: A $k$-sunflower is a family of $k$ distinct sets whose pairwise intersections all coincide. The Erd\H{o}s--Szemer\'edi conjecture asserts that for every $k \ge 3$ there is a constant $c_k < 2$ such that any $k$-sunflower-free family $\mathcal{F} \subseteq 2^{[n]}$ satisfies $|\mathcal{F}| \le c_k^{\,n}$. Bucic, He, and Lee recently proved this with an explicit bound.

In this talk we survey the problem and its place among sunflower questions, then work through the proof, centered on a vector-sunflower argument. We also discuss how the result relates to a related problem, the uniform Erd\H{o}s--Rado conjecture, which it does not settle. No prior background is assumed. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## #1 Proof of the Erdős-Szemerédi sunflower conjecture [PDF^{}] [Copy] [Kimi^{}] [REL]

Authors: Matija Bucić, Fankang He, Hyunwoo Lee

In the 1970s, Erdős and Szemerédi conjectured that for any $n \ge k-1\ge 2$, any collection of subsets of $[n]$ not containing a $k$-sunflower has size at most $c_k^n$ for some $c_k<2$. In the $k=3$ case, this follows from the work of Croot, Lev, and Pach and Ellenberg and Gijswijt on the cap-set problem, through a reduction due to Alon, Shpilka, and Umans. We prove the conjecture for every $k \ge 3$.

Subject: Combinatorics

citeturn196search3 [wordlim: 200] Published: 2 months ago; Crawled: last month; The Erdős–Sós problem [12] asks for the largest size of a family \(\mathcal {F} \subseteq \left( {\begin{array}{c}[n]\\ k\end{array}}\right) \) that avoids intersection size \(\ell \), and the Duke–Erdős problem [10] asks for the largest size of a family \(\mathcal {F} \subseteq \left( {\begin{array}{c}[n]\\ k\end{array}}\right) \) with no sunflower with m petals whose kernel has size \(\ell \). ... Recently, Bradač, Bucić, and Sudakov [6] managed to show that for the Duke–Erdős problem the answer is \(\Theta _k\big (n^{\max (\ell ,k-\ell -1)}m^{\min (k-\ell ,\ell +1)}\big )\); see also [30] for more refined results when \(k \ge 2\ell +3\).
Recently, Bradač, Bucić, and Sudakov [6] managed to show that for the Duke–Erdős problem the answer is \(\Theta _k\big (n^{\max (\ell ,k-\ell -1)}m^{\min (k-\ell ,\ell +1)}\big )\); see also [30] for more refined results when \(k \ge 2\ell +3\).

Using Theorem 1.2 for \(L=\{\ell \}\), it is easy to see that when \(\ell \in [k-1]\), then the answer for the m-petal Duke–Erdős problem is at most a factor of \(O_k(m^{k-\ell })\) times bigger than the answer for the Erdős–Sós problem. Indeed, if \(\mathcal {F}\subseteq \left( {\begin{array}{c}[n]\\ k\end{array}}\right) \) contains no sunflower with m petals and kernel size \(\ell \), then by Theorem 1.2, there is a subfamily \(\mathcal {F}'\subseteq \mathcal {F}\) with \(|\mathcal {F}'|=\Omega _k(m^{-k+\ell } |\mathcal {F}|)\) that avoids intersections of size \(\ell \). In particular, the result of Frankl and Füredi [17] mentioned above implies an upper bound of \(O_k(n^{\max (\ell ,k-\ell -1)} m^{k-\ell })\) for the m-petal problem if \(\ell \ge 1\). We note that in the proof of Bradač, Bucić, and Sudakov [6] of the general bound \(\Theta _k(n^{\max (\ell ,k-\ell -1)}m^{\min (k-\ell ,\ell +1)})\), the “balanced” case \(\ell =(k-1)/2\) plays an important role, since all other cases can be reduced to the balanced case. Notably, the above connection recovers their result when \(\ell \ge (k-1)/2\), which includes the “balanced” case.

To obtain our lower bound in Theorem 1.2, we use a technique that we call colour certificates. To demonstrate how colourings can be useful, consider a family \(\mathcal {F} \subseteq \left( {\begin{array}{c}[n]\\ k\end{array}}\right) \). We want to find a large subfamily \(\mathcal {F}'\subseteq \mathcal {F}\) with the property that for all A with \(|A|\in L\) we have some special element \(\varphi (A)\in [n]\setminus A\) such that for all \(F\in \mathcal {F}'\),

$$\begin{aligned} \text {if } A\subseteq F \text { then } \varphi (A)\in F. \end{aligned}$$
